territorial_scope.description: Applies to any person that owns, operates or otherwise makes available a companion AI chatbot to individuals in the United States, which can reach providers outside the United States.

evidence.quote: means any person that owns, operates, or otherwise makes available a companion AI chatbot to individuals in the United States.

agora_applications: Arts, sports, leisure, travel, and lifestyle

summary.short: Bill requiring any person making a companion AI chatbot available to individuals in the United States to require accounts, verify ages, protect minors via parental affiliation and consent, monitor suicidal ideation, and show not-human popups; FTC enforcement and state AG suits; effective one year after enactment.
summary.long: The bill would require covered entities, defined as any person that owns, operates or otherwise makes available a companion AI chatbot to individuals in the United States, to require user accounts; to verify the age of new account holders; to freeze existing accounts on the date described in section 7 until age information is provided; and to classify users as minors or adults. For minors, covered entities must affiliate the account with a verified parental account, obtain verifiable parental consent, immediately inform the parental account holder of suicidal ideation interactions, and block access to chatbots that engage in sexually explicit communication. Covered entities must limit age data collection and use to what is strictly necessary, monitor interactions for suicidal ideation and provide National Suicide Prevention Lifeline contact information, and display a popup at the start of each interaction and not less frequently than every 60 minutes stating the user is not engaging with a human. The FTC must issue compliance guidance within 180 days of enactment. Violations are treated as violations of an unfair or deceptive practices rule, enforced by the FTC and by state attorneys general through civil actions seeking injunctions, compliance, or damages. A safe harbor applies to entities that relied in good faith on user-provided age information, followed FTC guidance, and conformed to industry or FTC-identified standards. The Act takes effect one year after enactment.

notes: Introduced bill text. No relations to registry instruments were identified; all targets are external (target_instrument_id empty). Sec. 3(c)(3) uses 'parental account' and Sec. 3(d) uses 'verifiable parental consent' without defining them. Sec. 4(b) limits enforcement based on guidance, and Sec. 6 safe harbor refers to compliance with Sec. 4 guidance. Sec. 5 states no civil penalty amounts; penalties follow the FTC Act as incorporated. Sec. 3(b)(1) freezes existing accounts on the Sec. 7 date, one year after enactment.
